data.description: Elevation allows elements to be lifted from the background. It can be defined by applying drop shadows or other visual cues, such as color and borders

shadows.description: Elevation using shadows reflects a spatial relationship by indicating separation from the background or allowing content to be scrolled under another element.

levels.name: Shadow Low
levels.description: Subtle 2px vertical offset with 4px blur at 10% black opacity. Provides minimal lift for low-emphasis elements.

levels.name: Shadow Medium
levels.description: Medium elevation with 4px vertical offset and 24px blur at ~20% black opacity. Standard floating elements.

levels.name: Shadow High
levels.description: High elevation with 7px vertical offset and 32px blur at ~35% black opacity. Prominent overlays and tooltips.

levels.name: Shadow Stack Low
levels.description: Multi-layered stacked shadow with subtle opacity gradations creating depth perception. Five shadow layers from minimal to subtle.

levels.name: Elevated Dropdown
levels.description: Multi-layer shadow for dropdown menus and command palettes. Creates pronounced lift with multiple blur layers.

levels.name: Card Shadow
levels.description: Multi-layer shadow for cards with subtle depth. Three layers creating soft, natural elevation.

levels.name: Pressed Effect
levels.description: Tight shadow for pressed or inset appearance with 0.5px vertical offset at 30% black opacity.

levels.name: Focus Ring
levels.description: Solid border-like shadow using 0-blur spread for focus states. Uses brand indigo color.

levels.name: Subtle Border Ring
levels.description: Thin 0.5px border-like shadow for subtle separation between elements.
